angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 100,499,431 km at 91.41 pc = 14.7 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92862: distance 91.408 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.011), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 91.408 +/- 1.005 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 10.4404 +/- 0.2636 mas (same row, RUWE 2.95), 39.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 144.458 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92862: radius 144.458 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 2398.17 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.075) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 100,499,431 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3363 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92862: effective temperature 3363 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.074) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92862: effective temperature 3363 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.074) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 175865) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
